descriptionAr: اختبار تقييمي مجاني وشامل على الوحدة التاسعة: قصص النجاة والإرادة. ينشّط مهارات القواعد والمفردات والأسئلة الوزارية والقطع لمنهاج High Note 11.
descriptionEn: Free diagnostic unit exam for Unit 9: Survival & Human Will covering reading comprehension, vocabulary, and grammar in High Note 11.
text: Indonesian teenager, Aldi Adilang, is only 19, but he has already gone through the ordeal of being lost at sea an incredible three times! The first two times he got off relatively lightly; he was drifting for a week, and the second time for two days. However, on the third occasion, he was alone in the ocean for 49 long days. From when he was 16 years old, Aldi had spent weeks at a time working on a fishing trap, known as a rompong. This is a kind of hut which floats in the middle of the sea but is attached to the sea bed with a rope. Every night he would light lamps to attract the fish to his nets. It was a lonely kind of life. One day, the rope attaching his rompong to the bottom of the sea broke and he started to drift even further away from the coast. At first, he wasn’t too worried. He took it for granted that his boss would come and rescue him, as he had done before. Aldi had a week’s supply of food and was sure it would all be fine. But after a week, his supplies ran out. He caught fish and used parts of his wooden hut to make a fire and cook them. Having no more fresh drinking water, he had no choice but to drink sea water. However, he filtered the sea water through his clothes to reduce the amount of salt. This must have done the trick because he survived for four days until it rained and he was able to collect some rainwater. His survival skills were keeping him alive, but he was starting to wonder if he would ever be rescued. He saw more than ten ships sail past him, but none of them seemed to have a clue that he was there. After a few weeks, he thought he had at last got his lucky break when he managed to talk to the captain of an Indonesian ship. The captain promised he would pick him up, but heartbreakingly, Aldi never saw the ship again. After this setback, he really started to worry. To try and take his mind off his situation, he sang and read. The isolation took its toll on him, and he almost gave up hope, but the thought of seeing his parents again kept him going. In the end, after 49 days, he saw a ship called The Arpeggio. Desperate to be understood, he used the few words of English he knew: "Help! Help!". The ship turned around and rescued him. Safely back home, Aldi considered his options. His job was relatively lucrative at $134 a month, but having drifted three times, he and his family decided it simply wasn't worth the risk. From now on, he will stay firmly on dry land.

choices: Because the job was too dangerous after his terrifying ordeal.
Because he found a better paying job on a larger ship.
Because the floating trap was destroyed and could not be replaced.
Because he wanted to move to a different country.

choices: By building a makeshift sail and using a signaling mirror.
By swimming towards passing ships and shouting for help.
By catching fish to eat and filtering sea water through his clothes to drink.
By sending distress signals using a radio and waiting for rescue.

questions.question: The neighborhood is filled with ________ residents who often donate large sums to charity.
"If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam last year." The function of this Third Conditional sentence is:
choices: To talk about a present condition affecting a past result.
To describe a possible future event.
To describe an unreal or hypothetical situation in the past.
To state a general fact that is always true.

choices: To talk about a past habit.
To describe a real and likely future event.
To describe an unreal or hypothetical situation in the present or future.

choices: Mental strength prevents panic and helps a person make rational decisions to survive.

questions.question: When you touch a hot stove, you ________ your hand.

questions.question: The company’s new marketing strategy was a complete ________ ; it didn't increase sales at all.
